subject: Dedicated capacity: Nimble Robotics workload sizing & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimble-robotics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@nimble-robotics.com>, procurement@nimble-robotics.com
Date: Sat, 14 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — sample workload and questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We pulled together a short sample of production traffic and a few high-level asks so we can get a committed capacity proposal from Redwood. Quick summary of our product pattern:
- ~11M monthly requests (webhooks + batch inference).
- Average request size: 120 tokens prompt + 30 tokens response (150 tokens total).
- Typical session length (context): 2.2k tokens for multi-step dialogs, 95th pct 6k tokens.
- Peak concurrency target: 275 concurrent request contexts (we expect some requests to stream).
- SLA requirement: p95 gen latency < 250ms for user-facing endpoints during peak.

Could you confirm what GPU pool sizing you’d recommend (GPU type/count), an expected throughput guarantee at steady-state, and rough committed pricing options (12 vs 24 months)? I attached the sample CSV with RPS by hour and a short notebook output.

Also flagging that procurement will want a line item for burst capacity and a clause for cross-region failover.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimble Robotics
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimble-robotics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — sample workload and questions

Hi Alicia — thanks for the workbook and clear numbers. High-level takeaways after an initial pass:

- Workload profile: mixture of short single-turn webhooks (~60% of traffic) and longer multi-step sessions (~40%) with heavy KV/cache reuse. The 95th context length (6k tokens) is the cost driver here.
- Bottleneck: KV cache memory and attention compute on long sequences. For user-facing p95 latency <250ms we recommend a solution that keeps most hot sessions in memory and uses streaming where responses are longer.

Preliminary recommendation (ballpark, subject to full perf pass):
- GPU type: H100 (preferred) or A100-80GB as fallback.
- Minimum pool: 6x H100 (or 8x A100-80GB) dedicated behind a low-latency router. This yields ~300 concurrent short-context streams with autoscale headroom for bursts.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline reserve for 220 concurrent steady sessions with p95 < 250ms. We can commit to 220 steady concurrency at the proposed pool size. Bursts handled by short-term over-provisioning (burst credits) and fallback to slightly higher-latency model variants.
- Token throughput estimate: ~9.5M tokens/sec aggregate at steady-state (model/mix dependent).

Pricing notes (initial):
- 12-month commit: list price with a 18% committed discount on Dedicated hourly + 10% credit toward burst usage.
- 24-month commit: deeper discount — 26% off list + extended burst credits (20% of monthly committed hours).

I'll loop in Marcus for a more detailed sizing calc and Ben to draft the pricing sheet. Can you confirm if cross-region failover needs a hot standby (always-on in EU) or cold-standby (bring-up on failover)? That affects the pricing materially.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimble-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — sample workload and questions

Alicia, Sofia — I ran a focused sizing calc against the CSV you attached. Summary (concise):

Assumptions we used:
- Model: open-mix (primary generation model quantized) — token cost ~0.28 GPU-ms/token on H100 for the long-context mix.
- Avg request tokens: 150; p95 sessions 6k tokens but represent 40% of compute due to attention-cost scaling ~O(n^2) on memory-bound kernels.
- Effective concurrency target: steady 220, peak 275.

Sizing result (safe configuration):
- 6x H100 (DGX-style pooling) with 1.6TB aggregate NVMe + 1.4TB shared KV cache recommended.
- Expected p95 latency at steady 220: ~180–230ms (depends on small model tweaks). At peak 275 expect p95 to be ~260–320ms unless burst credits are used.
- If Nimble requires strict p95 <250ms at peak 275, recommend 8x H100 (adds ~22% capacity).

Pricing scenarios: (rounded, USD/month)
- 12-mo commit @ 6x H100: $365k/month list -> committed price ~$299k/month after 18% discount. Burst credits handled at discounted overage rate.
- 24-mo commit @ 6x H100: $270k/month after 26% discount (annualized).
- 12-mo commit @ 8x H100 (if you need peak p95 hard): $420k/mo list -> ~$344k/mo committed.

We can trade some of the up-front discount for additional burst credits or a shorter SLA escalation window. Ben, please attach a granular cost table and the SOW stub.

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimble-robotics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — sample workload and questions

Alicia — attaching the proposed quote and SOW draft (see attachments). Highlights:
- Option A (6x H100): commit 12 months -> $299k/mo committed rate, includes 10% burst credit (hours).
- Option B (6x H100): commit 24 months -> $270k/mo committed rate, includes 20% burst credit and one free DR failover test per year.
- Option C (8x H100): commit 12 months -> $344k/mo committed rate, includes 10% burst credit.

Negotiation levers we can offer:
- Swap a portion of the discount into professional services hours (benchmarked onboarding) if procurement prefers fewer line items.
- Multi-year price floor instead of upfront commit to lower CAPEX sensitivity.

Alicia — procurement asked earlier about cross-region failover type. You mentioned potentially cold-standby — if that’s the case we can include cold-standby for an additional $7k/mo (reserve capacity without hot cache). Hot standby (warm replication + streaming) is materially higher.

Please let us know target committee date for procurement so we can align the proposal and finalize DocuSign.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-NIMBLE-v1.pdf, SOW_draft_nimble_v2.docx)
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@nimble-robotics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@nimble-robotics.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@nimble-robotics.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — sample workload and questions

Ben / Sofia / Marcus —

Thank you — this is exactly what procurement needed to start the internal committee review. A few follow-ups:
- Procurement prefers the 24-month commit if we can secure the $270k/mo and a fixed price floor for year 3. Can Redwood do a 24-month with a year-3 price floor (no more than +5% YoY)?
- Cold-standby looks acceptable as an initial posture; we’ll request a warm-replication pilot during Q4 if performance warrants.
- Can you add a line item for privacy & audit support (SOC2 evidence package) and a one-time security review fee? We’ll need the SOC2 artifact and a 3rd-party pen-test report in the SOW.

If you can send an updated quote and a clean SOW we’ll circulate to the committee next week.

— Tom
Tom Reed
VP Operations, Nimble Robotics
